comments.body:
## DECISION NEEDED — narrow `error_code_for` so `llm_unavailable` means a real outage only

**The change.** Make `llm_unavailable` fire ONLY for `LLMUnavailableError` (the true transient-outage type); every other `LLMError` subclass falls to its explicit `error_code` attribute, else the honest broad `command_failed`.

**This finishes an established direction, it does not open a new one.** Bug `f75f` already carved `LLMRunnerError → command_failed` out of the blanket `LLMError → llm_unavailable` (`_llm_error_code`, `_errors.py:110-127`). What remains is the residual over-claim: the bare `LLMError` base and non-availability subclasses still map to `llm_unavailable` (`:126-127`). ce6b removes that residual — the systematic completion of epic `3405`'s descriptiveness intent — and delivers `551b`'s ruling (editor missing-bundle → `command_failed`).

**OSS grounding.** Same gRPC/HTTP principle as 73d8: reserve `UNAVAILABLE`/503 for genuine outages so retry, backoff, and alerting semantics stay meaningful. An over-broad "unavailable" triggers pointless retries and poisons outage dashboards.

**Risk is low and bounded** because the fix is required to enumerate every `LLMError` subclass and add held-out tests proving (a) a genuine execute-time outage still returns `llm_unavailable` and (b) a non-outage `WorkflowError` (e.g. editor missing-bundle at `editor.py:475`) returns `command_failed`.

**Recommendation:** Approve. Land ce6b as the umbrella and fold **73d8**'s `ExpressionError → invalid_input` into the same sweep (set its explicit `error_code`) so the two changes are consistent. Keep the finer `environment_unready` code DEFERRED per 551b's stated trigger.

compiled_state.description:
Spun from 73d8-4871-1b49-4047 (brainy-convulsant-unicorn) and 551b-1a30-ac2b-4127 (sanidine-cilium-eland) during the 2026-08-30 error-code decision pass.

## Problem
`error_code_for` (`src/rebar/_errors.py`) maps the broad `LLMError` family to `llm_unavailable`. That over-claims an AI-provider outage for non-outage faults: the bare `LLMError` base, concrete LLM/workflow subclasses that are not in the provider-unavailability subtree, and the editor missing-bundle failure that currently raises a bare `WorkflowError`. This is the residual of origin 8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239's blanket mapping and the systematic completion of epic 3405-c0b7-0436-4b46's descriptiveness intent.

## Operator decision
The latest DECISION NEEDED comment approves narrowing `llm_unavailable` to true LLM availability failures while preserving dbca AC3's compatibility contract: a genuine outage surfaced through the bare `WorkflowError` execute-wrapper contract still reads as `llm_unavailable`. The implementation keeps `isinstance(exc, LLMUnavailableError) -> llm_unavailable`, intentionally including `LLMConfigError` / prompt / reviewer configuration subclasses because those classes inherit from `LLMUnavailableError` and model missing LLM dependencies, credentials, or configuration. The implementation removes the broad catch-all for all other `LLMError` instances.

The split between dbca AC3 and the editor missing-bundle case is type-based, not message-based. The bare `WorkflowError` base remains `llm_unavailable` as the legacy execute-outage wrapper contract. The editor missing-bundle raise at `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:475` will stop using bare `WorkflowError`; it will raise a dedicated `WorkflowAssetsUnavailableError(WorkflowError)` with `error_code = "command_failed"`. That delivers 551b's ruled behavior without message sniffing and without changing the dbca AC3 bare-base contract. Do not add `environment_unready`.

Ticket 73d8-4871-1b49-4047 is folded into this sweep by giving `ExpressionError` an explicit `error_code = "invalid_input"`, matching prior bug 35ab-f0e0-3e4a-4b72 (unknown-step -> invalid_input) and dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d (parse/lint -> invalid_input).

## Implementation scope
Touch `src/rebar/_errors.py`, `src/rebar/llm/errors.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py`, `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py`, and tests. Enumerate every concrete subclass of `LLMError` across `src/rebar/llm/`, including `errors.py`, `findings.py`, `evals/eval.py`, `prompting/`, and `workflow/`, with Serena hierarchy/reference checks and a grep/string confirmation. Update the existing pinned contract tests that currently assert the blanket mapping: `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_error_code_taxonomy_contract.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_llmrunner_error_codes_f75f_heldout.py`, `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_35ab.py`, and `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py`.

Intended mapping: `LLMUnavailableError` and its availability/config subtree -> `llm_unavailable`; bare `WorkflowError` base -> `llm_unavailable` for the preserved dbca execute-outage wrapper contract; `WorkflowAssetsUnavailableError` -> `command_failed`; `ExpressionError` -> `invalid_input`; workflow caller/authoring errors already classified as `invalid_input` stay there; every remaining non-availability LLM/findings/eval/snapshot subclass without an explicit `error_code` -> `command_failed`; bare `LLMError` base -> `command_failed`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `src/rebar/_errors.py` returns `llm_unavailable` for `LLMUnavailableError` / `LLMConfigError` availability errors and preserves bare `WorkflowError` base -> `llm_unavailable` for the dbca execute-outage compatibility contract; focused tests verify these mappings.
- [x] A dedicated editor missing-bundle exception raised from `src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor.py:475` maps to `command_failed`, not `llm_unavailable`, and no message sniffing is used.
- [x] The broad `LLMError` base and every non-availability `LLMError` subclass except the deliberately preserved bare `WorkflowError` base maps to an explicit `error_code` when present, otherwise `command_failed`; a parameterized taxonomy test covers the complete enumerated subclass set.
- [x] `ExpressionError` maps to `invalid_input` via an explicit `error_code`, verified by a focused test and by the exhaustive taxonomy test.
- [x] No `environment_unready` code is introduced; `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` remains consistent with the intentional taxonomy.

## Testing
Run the focused updated contract tests with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/interfaces/contracts/test_error_code_taxonomy_contract.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_llmrunner_error_codes_f75f_heldout.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_35ab.py tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py`, then `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`. After committing, run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" rebar verify-commit-ticket HEAD`.

File-impact update after implementation: this ticket is closed by the combined Gerrit #2482 commit, whose actual reviewed diff also exports the new dedicated workflow asset-unavailable exception from `src/rebar/llm/__init__.py`; that export is intentional so all LLM public error types remain reachable from the package facade.
